name: A Bismarck street

place_source.title: Wikidata: Bismarck (Q37066), coordinate location and elevation above sea level

blurb: One city block of Bismarck, North Dakota: a grass boulevard between elm and green ash, juniper and spruce on the verges, hawthorn along the lot lines, and a June lawn that thirteen-lined ground squirrels tunnel through. Robins, sparrows, goldfinches and flickers work it by day; fox squirrels cross overhead; a red-tailed hawk takes the tallest pole.

facts.text: Bismarck sits in the middle of the Great Plains and has a highly variable four-season humid continental climate, with cold, dry, snowy, windy winters and warm, humid summers.

source.title: Wikipedia contributors, "Bismarck, North Dakota", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Bismarck, North Dakota", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: January averages -10.7 °C and July averages 21.8 °C, so the warmest month on that city's own figures sits just under the 22 °C that separates Koppen Dfa from Dfb; the class recorded here is Dfb.

source.title: Wikipedia contributors, "Bismarck, North Dakota", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Bismarck, North Dakota", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Precipitation peaks from May to September and is rather sparse in the winter; winter snowfall is typically light to moderate and major storms are rare.

source.title: Wikipedia contributors, "Bismarck, North Dakota", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Bismarck, North Dakota", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Bismarck is the capital of North Dakota and the county seat of Burleigh County, and was North Dakota's second-most populous city at the 2020 census, with 73,622 residents.

source.title: Wikipedia contributors, "Bismarck, North Dakota", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Bismarck, North Dakota", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: It was founded in 1872 on the east bank of the Missouri River and became the capital of the Dakota Territory in 1883 and of the new state in 1889; Mandan sits across the river, and together the two make one metropolitan area.

source.title: Wikipedia contributors, "Bismarck, North Dakota", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Bismarck, North Dakota", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: Green ash is native to eastern and central North America, from Nova Scotia west to southeastern Alberta and eastern Colorado and south to Oklahoma and eastern Texas, which covers North Dakota; it is also the commonest street tree in the catalog here.

source.title: Wikipedia contributors, "Fraxinus pennsylvanica", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Fraxinus pennsylvanica", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: The American elm is a very hardy species that can withstand low winter temperatures, and was once exceptionally common as a street tree, its tolerance of urban conditions making it a popular choice to line American streets.

source.title: Wikipedia contributors, "Ulmus americana", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Ulmus americana", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0

facts.text: White spruce is native south to Montana, North Dakota, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan and Vermont, which is why a cold-hardy spruce stands in a Bismarck winter street here.

source.title: Wikipedia contributors, "Picea glauca", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
source.attribution: Wikipedia contributors, "Picea glauca", English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0
